Rashi on Zevachim 2b:3:2.hebrew: לא הוית גבן באורתא בתחומא: כלומר, חבל על שלא היית אמש בשבת אצלנו בתוך התחום שתוכל לבוא לבית המדרש ולשמוע.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:10:1.hebrew: דל עובדת כוכבים מיניה - ואימא נמי דלאו מינה לא מחריב בה, אפילו הכי פסול, דהוה ליה סתמא, דמיהו לאו לשם אשה זו נכתב:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:10:1.english: Remove the gentile woman from it - And say also that it is not from her, [and] he does not destroy [the marriage] through it; even so, it is invalid, for it is [then] unspecified, since in any case it was not written for the sake of this woman.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:10:2.hebrew: דל חולין מינייהו - כדסבירא לן דלא חייל ולא מחריב ביה, דלא מיניה הוה. הוו להו שחוטין סתם, ואמרן לעיל סתמא כשירה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:10:2.english: Remove non-sacred from them - As we hold, that it (the non-sacred intent) does not take effect and does not invalidate it, since it is not of its kind. They become animals slaughtered without specification, and we said above that without specification is fit.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:12:1.hebrew: תוכו - כתוב "כל כלי חרס וגו'" (ויקרא יא), ולא תוך תוכו. כגון כלי המונח בתנור ופיו למעלה מן פי התנור, ואוכלין ומשקין בתוכו, ושרץ בתנור — אוכלין שבכלים טהורין. והכי אמרינן בת"כ: אבל היה פיו בתוך התנור — תוכו קרינן ביה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:12:1.english: Its interior - The verse states: "Every earthen vessel, etc." (Leviticus 11), but not the interior of its interior. For example, a vessel placed in an oven with its mouth higher than the mouth of the oven, with foods and liquids inside it, and a creeping animal is in the oven — the foods in the vessels are pure. And so we say in the Torat Kohanim: But if its mouth was inside the oven, we call it "its interior."

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:12:2.hebrew: ואפי' כלי שטף מציל - כלומר, לא מיבעיא כלי חרס המונח בתנור דמציל על האוכלין שבתוכו, דהא תוך תוכו הוא, וכלי גופיה ליכא למימר דמיטמא באויר ויטמא אוכלין שבו, דאין כלי חרס מיטמא מגבו. אלא אפי' כלי שטף, שמיטמא מגבו, הכא טהור ומציל. דאמר התנא [בפ' קמא דפסחים] (דף כ:) אוכלין מיטמאים מאויר כלי חרס, ואין כלי מיטמא מאויר כלי חרס. ומדקתני כלי שטף מציל, אלמא דלאו מיניה חייץ ביה [ומבטל את שם תוכו], הכא נמי ליחול שם חולין וליפסל:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:12:2.english: And even a vessel that is rinsed protects - That is to say: It is not necessary to say that an earthenware vessel placed inside an oven protects the food inside it, for it is the interior of its interior; and as for the vessel itself, one cannot say that it becomes impure through the airspace and thereby renders impure the food within it, since an earthenware vessel does not become impure from its outer side. Rather, even a vessel that is rinsed, which does become impure from its outer side, is here pure and protects. For it is stated [in the first chapter of Pesachim] (20b): Foods become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel, but a vessel does not become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel. And since it teaches that a vessel that is rinsed protects, evidently, even a vessel that is not of the same kind serves as a partition within it [and nullifies the status of its interior]. Here too, then, the status of non-sacred food should take effect on the meat and it should become disqualified:

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:13:1.hebrew: ושני הכא עשו חולין אצל קדשים כו' - כלומר, לעולם דלאו מינה לאו מחריב ביה, וכלי שטף אצל כלי חרס מיניה הוא, דהא מנא והא מנא. אבל חולין אצל קדשים הוי דלאו מיניה, כמחיצה אצל תנור דאמרינן ביה לקמן דלא מהניא ביה להיות חציצה בין שרץ לאוכלין, כדאמרן דלאו מיניה לא מחריב בה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:13:1.english: And the second one here: they made non-sacred [meat] relative to sacrificial animals, etc. - That is to say: Indeed, [something] that is not of its type does not destroy it; and a vessel [purified by] rinsing relative to an earthenware vessel is of its type, for this is a vessel and that is a vessel. But non-sacred [meat] relative to sacrificial animals is [considered] not of its type, like a partition relative to an oven, concerning which we say below that it is not effective in it to be a barrier between a creeping creature and the foodstuffs, as we said: [something] that is not of its type does not destroy it.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:14:1.hebrew: שחצצו בנסרים - שעשה מחיצה באמצעו, וחלקו עד למעלה מפיו. הכל טמא — אפילו אוכלין שבעבר השני של מחיצה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:14:1.english: That one divided with boards - That he made a partition in its middle and divided it up to above its mouth. All is impure — even food that is on the other side of the partition.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:15:1.hebrew: כוורת שהיא פחותה - גרסינן בטהרות. ולהכי נקט "פחותה", דלאו כלי הוא; דאי הואי שלימה, הוה מצלת על אוכלין שבתוכה, כדאמרן: אפי' כלי שטף מציל. אבל השתא דלאו כלי הוא, הויא כמחיצה בעלמא:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:15:1.english: A barrel that is broken - We read this in Taharot. And the reason he said "broken" is that it is not a vessel; for if it were whole, it would protect the food inside it, as we said: even a keli shetef — a vessel of wood, leather, or cloth, which can contract impurity and is purified by rinsing in water — protects. But now that it is not a vessel, it is merely like a partition.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:15:2.hebrew: ופקוקה בקש - רבותא נקט, דאע"ג דפקוקה פחיתתה בקש, לא הוי כלי, ואפי' פיה למעלה מפי תנור, לא מצלת על אוכלין שבתוכה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:15:2.english: And plugged up with straw - [The Mishnah] states a novelty: even though its breach is plugged up with straw, it is not considered a vessel, and even if its mouth is above the mouth of the oven, it does not protect the food that is inside it.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:15:4.hebrew: אוכלין שבתוכה טמאים - והיינו דאמרן, דלא מינה, כגון מחיצה, לא מחריב בה לבטל שם תוכו ממנו:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:15:4.english: The food inside it is impure - And this is what we said: that which is not of its kind, such as a partition, one does not destroy with it, so as to nullify from it the name "its interior."

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:1:1.english: And reconsidered - Not to divorce her.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:2:1.hebrew: דילמא שאני התם - דלאו סתמא הוא, אלא שלא לשמה ממש:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:2:1.english: Perhaps there it is different - For it is not [a case of] unspecified [intent], but rather actual [intent] not for her sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:2:2.hebrew: דאינתיק - משאר כל האנשים והנשים, [לשם] גירושין של זה ושל זו:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:2:2.english: That it was detached - From all other men and women, [for the sake of] the divorce of this [man] and this [woman].

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:5:1.hebrew: אלא מהא - דעדיפא מקמייתא, דהכא חד גברא הוא:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:5:1.english: Rather, from this — Which is preferable to the former [case], as here it is one man.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:6:1.hebrew: דאין ברירה - וגריעה מסתמא, דשמא בשעה שנכתב לא היה בדעתו של בעל לזו, ואינתק לשם האחרת:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:6:1.english: For there is no retroactive designation - And [this case] is worse than [one done] without specification, for perhaps at the time it was written, it was not in the husband's mind [to write it] for this [wife], and it was diverted for the sake of the other [wife].

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:7:1.hebrew: הכותב טופסי גיטין - שיהו מזומנין לו. טופס — לשון טפוס, מול"ל בלע"ז:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:7:1.english: One who writes the standard forms of bills of divorce - [He does so] so that they will be ready for him. Tofes is an expression of tefus [a form/pattern], moule [mold/template] in Old French.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:7:2.hebrew: מקום הרי את כו' - דזהו עיקר גופו. אלמא סתמא פסול, ואף על גב דאיכתב לשם כריתות לכשיזדמן לו:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:7:2.english: The place of "You are hereby," etc. - For this is the essence of its core text. Evidently, [writing] without specification is invalid, even though it was written for the purpose of severance for when [a case] should present itself to him.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:8:1.hebrew: תו רמי מילתא אחריתי - אדרבינא ורב פפא קאי, דקאמר דרמי רבא אהדדי ושנינהו:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:8:1.english: He further raised another contradiction - [This] refers back to [the exchange between] Ravina and Rav Pappa, where [Ravina] said that Rava contrasted [statements] against each other and resolved them:

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:8:2.hebrew: דרב יהודה אמר רב - לקמן בפרק בית שמאי (זבחים דף מו:):
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:8:2.english: That Rav Yehudah said Rav - Later, in the chapter Beit Shammai (Zevachim 46b).

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:8:3.hebrew: לשם חולין כשירה - קס"ד סברא דידיה היא, כדמפרש רבא: דמינה מחריב בה — דבר שהוא מינו מועיל בו לעקור את שמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:8:3.english: [If one slaughtered it] for the sake of non-sacred [meat], it is fit - The initial assumption is that this is [Rav’s] own reasoning, as [Rava] explains: “that of its own type ruins it” — something that is of its own type is effective with regard to it to uproot its name.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:8:4.hebrew: דלאו מינה - כגון חולין, שאינו מין קדשים, לא מחריב בה, ואין שמו נתפס על הזבח לעקור שמו ממנו:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:8:4.english: That is not of its type - For example, non-sacred [meat], which is not a type of sacred offering, does not ruin it, and its name does not take hold upon the offering so as to uproot its [proper] name from it.

Rashi on Zevachim 3a:9:1.hebrew: ואפי' לשם עובדת כוכבים - דהא "שלא לשם האשה" קתני, דמשמע שלא לשם אשה זו, אלא לשום אשה אחרת כל דהו. ואע"ג דעובדת כוכבים לאו בת גירושין היא, מהניא לפסול. אלמא דלאו מינה היא [מחריב] בה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3a:9:1.english: And even for the sake of a gentile woman - For it teaches "not for the sake of the woman," which implies not for the sake of this woman, but for the sake of any other woman whatsoever. And even though a gentile woman is not one who can be divorced, her name is effective to invalidate [the get]. Evidently, she is not of the same type [as a Jewish woman, and yet it invalidates it].

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: Rava’s discourse was on Shabbat night, and Rav Pappa was not able to attend because he was outside the Shabbat limit (Rashi).

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 3a:8.english: The Rambam rules that although a Pesach offering is similar to a sin offering in that both are disqualified if they are slaughtered for the sake of the wrong offering, a Pesach offering that is slaughtered for the sake of non-sacred meat is disqualified, whereas a sin offering is not. This ruling is derived in the Jerusalem Talmud from the verse: “It is the offering of the Lord’s Passover” (Exodus 12:27). The Rambam also writes that in a case where a sin offering was slaughtered for the sake of non-sacred meat, although the sin offering is fit, it does not satisfy the obligation of its owner. The Ramban (Milĥamot HaShem on tractate Rosh HaShana) maintains that it does satisfy the obligation of the owner (see Rambam’s Commentary on the Mishna, and Sefer Avoda, Hilkhot Pesulei HaMukdashin 15:11).

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: This Aramaic expression generally refers to the statements of the Sages that were cited in the study hall. In several places in the Talmud, a Sage is cited as having requested that another Sage tell him the superior statements (*mili me'alyata*) of a certain Sage, e.g., Rav, Rav Ḥisda, or Rav Yosef, that were mentioned in the study hall. In other places it is stated that a Sage requested of his colleagues that certain superior statements be attributed to him. A Sage who was absent from the study hall was liable to miss superior statements that were conveyed at the time.

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Zevachim 3a:8.english: However, it did not satisfy the owner's obligation (Rambam). But the Ramban (in Milchamot HaShem on Tractate Rosh HaShana) holds that in a case where one slaughtered a sin offering for the sake of non-sacred meat, it did satisfy the owner's obligation.

Steinsaltz comment #3 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: A Shabbat limit is the border of a Jewish settlement or of the temporary residence of one or more Jews, determined at the onset of Shabbat. It is defined as two thousand cubits outside the residence. By rabbinic decree it is not permitted for a person to travel on Shabbat beyond this limit. On Shabbat Sages would leave their cities to deliver lectures and sermons in nearby villages. One’s ability to learn Torah on Shabbat was often dependent on his ability to travel to the locale to which the Sage would come without going beyond the Shabbat limit.

Steinsaltz comment #3 on Zevachim 3a:8.english: For something that is not of its type at all, such as non-sacred animals in relation to consecrated offerings, is not considered something that can be attached to it in order to uproot the name of the sin offering from it (Rashi).

Steinsaltz comment #4 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: This city, also called Ḥarmakh, or according to other readings, Harman or Bei Harman, was located on the Shanvata River. Some propose that the source of the name is the Persian word harman, meaning granary.

Steinsaltz comment #4 on Zevachim 3a:8.english: Later authorities wrote (see in Chazon Yechezkel and elsewhere) that from here it is proven that the primary disqualification when one changes its name from one sacred offering to another is not on the negative side, by uprooting its previous name, but on the positive side—that one designates this offering for another purpose. And therefore, it does not have the power to designate the purpose of a sin offering that was consecrated for the sake of non-sacred animals, which are not of its type at all.

Steinsaltz comment #5 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: Round wicker barrels were often used as beehives in antiquity. In modern Hebrew, the word kavveret means beehive.

Steinsaltz comment #5 on Zevachim 3a:8.english: A sin offering that was slaughtered for the sake of another offering (such as a burnt offering) — this is disqualified. But if one slaughtered it for the sake of non-sacred animals — this is fit, but it did not satisfy the owner's obligation. In accordance with Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav. (Rambam Sefer Avoda Hilkhot Pesulei HaMukdashin 15:4).

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 2b:3.english: Ravina said to Rav Pappa: Since you were not with us last night within the Shabbat limit of Bei Ḥarmakh, Rav Pappa did not hear that Rava raises a contradiction between two superior Mishnayot and teaches their resolution.

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 3a:11.english: And Rava raised another contradiction: Did Rav Yehuda say that Rav says that a sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is unfit, whereas if one slaughtered it for the sake of ordinary meat it is fit? Apparently, Rav holds that only improper intent that is of its type disqualifies it, whereas wrong intent that is not of its type does not disqualify it.

Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:12:1.hebrew: ורמינהו תוכו ולא תוך תוכו ואפי' כלי שטף מציל - מפרש בקונטרס: שרץ בחיצון ואוכלין בפנימי, לא מיבעיא כלי חרס דאין מיטמא מגבו, אלא אפי' כלי שטף דמיטמא מגבו — אין אוכלין שבתוכו [טמאים], שגם כלי שטף אינו מקבל טומאה מאויר כלי חרס, כדאמר בפ' קמא דפסחים (דף כ): אוכלין מקבלין טומאה מאויר כלי חרס, ואין כלים מקבלים טומאה מאויר כלי חרס. וקשה לפירושו, דאם כן מה חידוש יותר בכלי שטף מכלי חרס? ועוד, דאיכא חידוש יותר בכלי חרס, כגון אם שרץ באויר כלי חרס פנימי, ואוכלין בכלי חרס חיצון — טהורין, אע"פ שהפנימי טמא. ונראה לפרש דכל רבותא של כלי שטף היינו משום דלאו מינה הוא, וס"ד דלא מחריב בה, וטמא — קמ"ל שמציל [ודוקא בכלי שטף שאינו מינו היה טמא אי לאו קרא]. אבל תוך תוכו שהכל הוא של חרס מינו, פשיטא שהוא טהור בלא פסוק, דתוך דוקא אמר רחמנא. וכן מוכח לקמן דכלי שטף דוקא איצטריך קרא, דפריך: ומי אמר רבא חטאת ששחטה על מי שמחוייב עולה כשירה? אלמא לאו מינה לא מחריב בה! והתניא: תוכו ולא תוך תוכו ואפי' כלי שטף מציל. ומשני: ארבעה תוכו כתיבי, חד תוכו ולא תוך תוכו. פי': אפי' לא כתב אלא תוך, הוה מיעטנא כלי חרס פנימי שאין אוכלין שבתוכו מקבלין טומאה ע"י שרץ שבחיצון, שהרי אין השרץ תוכו. ודוקא כלי חרס פנימי, דהוי דומיא דידיה, מעיטנא, דמינה מחריב בה וחוצץ. להכי כתב וי"ו של תוכו, למימר דאפי' לאו מינה, כגון כלי שטף, מחריב בה ומציל. ותימה, אמאי לא שני בשמעתין נמי הכי? שאני התם, דאמר קרא תוכו ולא תוך תוכו, ולא איצטריך אלא לכלי שטף. וי"ל דעדיפא משני הכא, דקאי על חטאת לשם חולין כשירה, ועל זה תירץ: עשו חולין אצל קדשים דאינן מינם כלל, ולכך לא מחריב בה, כמחיצה אצל תנור, כמו מחיצה, וכמו כוורת הקש פחותה שאינה כלי כלל ואינה מצלת כלל. אבל כלי שטף קרוי מינו קצת, שיש לו שם כלי עליו, ולכך מחריב ומציל. אבל לקמן קאי על חטאת ששחטה לשם מחוייב עולה כשירה, דאע"ג שהוא קדשים, קרוי אינו מינו ולא מחריב בה, ועל זה פריך: מאי שנא מכלי שטף שהוא כלי ואינו מינו, ומחריב? ועל זה צריך לתרץ משום קרא תוכו ולא תוך תוכו, אבל לא מצי לתרץ עשוהו כמחיצה אצל תנור, דההוא אינו כלי כלל. והשתא הכא ולקמן מתרץ דומה בדומה (ודוקא בכלי שטף שאינו מינו היה טמא אי לאו קרא, אבל תוך שהכל חרס טהור בלא פסוק, דחד תוך אמר רחמנא):
Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:12:1.english: "Let us raise a contradiction: 'Its interior, but not the interior of its interior, and even a rinsing-vessel protects'" - Rashi explains: [The case is where] the creeping animal is in the outer [vessel] and the foodstuffs are in the inner one. Not only [if the inner vessel is] an earthenware vessel, which does not become impure from its outer surface, but even a rinsing-vessel (a vessel of metal or wood), which does become impure from its outer surface — the foodstuffs inside it [are not impure], for even a rinsing-vessel does not receive impurity from the airspace of an earthenware vessel, as is stated in the first chapter of Pesachim (20a): Foodstuffs receive impurity from the airspace of an earthenware vessel, but vessels do not receive impurity from the airspace of an earthenware vessel. But this is difficult according to his explanation: if so, what is the novelty in a rinsing-vessel more than in an earthenware vessel? Furthermore, there is a greater novelty in an earthenware vessel, for example, if a creeping animal is in the airspace of an inner earthenware vessel and foodstuffs are in an outer earthenware vessel — they are pure, even though the inner one is impure. It appears to explain that the entire novelty of a rinsing-vessel is because it is not of the same kind [as an earthenware vessel], and one might have thought that it does not nullify [the status of the interior of] the earthenware vessel, and [the food] would be impure; [the baraita] teaches us that it protects [and only with a rinsing-vessel, which is not of the same kind, would [the food] have been impure had it not been for the verse]. But with the interior of its interior, where everything is earthenware, of the same kind, it is obvious that it is pure even without a verse, since the Merciful One said "interior" specifically. And so it is proven later that the verse was needed specifically for a rinsing-vessel, for [the Gemara] asks: But did Rava really say that a sin offering slaughtered for the sake of one obligated to bring a burnt offering is valid? Evidently, [a thing] not of the same kind does not nullify it! But isn't it taught: "Its interior, but not the interior of its interior, and even a rinsing-vessel protects"? And [the Gemara] answers: "Its interior" is written four times; one is "its interior, but not the interior of its interior." Explanation: Even had [the Torah] written only "interior," I would have excluded an inner earthenware vessel, so that foodstuffs inside it do not receive impurity through a creeping animal in the outer one, since the creeping animal is not in its interior. And I would have excluded specifically an inner earthenware vessel, which is similar to it, because it is of its kind and so nullifies it and acts as a divider. Therefore [the Torah] wrote the vav of "tokho," to say that even [a vessel] not of its kind, such as a rinsing-vessel, nullifies it and protects. It is surprising: why did [the Gemara] not answer the same way in our passage as well? It is different there, because the verse says "its interior, but not the interior of its interior," and it was needed only for a rinsing-vessel. And one can say that the answer here is stronger, since it is addressing a sin offering [slaughtered] for the sake of a non-sacred offering being valid, and for this [the Gemara] answered: They made non-sacred items next to sacred items to be not of their kind at all, and therefore it does not nullify it, like a partition next to an oven — like a partition — and like a small straw beehive, which is not a vessel at all and does not protect at all. But a rinsing-vessel is called somewhat of its kind, since it has the name "vessel" upon it, and therefore it nullifies and protects. But later [the Gemara] is addressing a sin offering slaughtered for the sake of one obligated to bring a burnt offering, which is valid, for even though it is sacred, it is called not of its kind and does not nullify it; and on this [the Gemara] asks: How is it different from a rinsing-vessel, which is a vessel and not of its kind, yet nullifies? And for this it needs to answer because of the verse "its interior, but not the interior of its interior"; but it could not answer "they made it like a partition next to an oven," since that is not a vessel at all. And now, here and later, [the Gemara] answers [by comparing] like with like (and only with a rinsing-vessel, which is not of the same kind, would it have been impure had it not been for the verse; but with an interior where everything is earthenware, it is pure without a verse, since the Merciful One said "interior" once):

Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:1:1.hebrew: כתב לגרש את אשתו ונמלך כו' - תימה: מה ענין זה אצל סתם? ויש לומר דס"ד, כיון דנמלך — אם כן מסתמא כתבו מתחילה שאם יחזור בו, יגרש מי שירצה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:1:1.english: "He wrote [a bill of divorce] to divorce his wife and reconsidered, etc." - It is astonishing: What does this matter have to do with [an offering brought] unspecified? And one can say that it could enter your mind [to think] that since he reconsidered, if so, he presumably wrote it initially [with the intention] that if he reconsiders, he may divorce whomever he wishes.

Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:7:1.hebrew: הכותב טופסי גיטין כו' - כל הנך משניות בפ' כל הגט (גיטין דף כו.). ותימה, דלא קתני בהך "יתר על כן", דעל כרחין יתר הוא, דמכל הנך קמייתא לא מצי למידק סתמא פסול אלא מהך! ויש לומר, דמשום ד"אמר ללבלר" דקתני ברישא דהך — יתר כמו כן, דדייקינן מזאת [סתמא], ודייקינן מינה אין ברירה. וקשה לה"ר יצחק, דפ"ק דפסחים (דף יד.) תנן: "הוסיף ר"ע", אף ע"ג דלמאן דמוקי מילתא דר' חנינא בולד [וולד] הטומאה דרבנן, לא שמעינן לה ממילתיה דר' עקיבא, דמיירי בפסולא [דאורייתא]! מיהו יש לומר, אע"ג דקתני "הוסיף", אי לא הוה תני ליה לא הוה [קמשמע לן] מידי:
Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:7:1.english: "One who writes the standard parts of bills of divorce, etc." - All of these mishnayot are in the chapter [entitled] "Kol HaGet" (Gittin 26a). And it is surprising that [the Mishnah] did not teach in this [case]: "Furthermore" [yeter al ken], for perforce it is a greater novelty, since from all those earlier [cases] one could not deduce that an unspecified [writing of a bill of divorce] is invalid, except from this one! And one can say: because "He said to the scribe...", which is taught earlier than this one, is an addition as well, as we deduce from this [case that] [unspecified writing is invalid], and we deduce from it that there is no retroactive designation [bereirah]. And this was difficult to Rabbi Yitzchak: for in the first chapter of Pesachim (14a) we learned: "Rabbi Akiva added...", even though according to the one who establishes the matter of Rabbi Chanina as regarding an offspring of an offspring of defilement of Rabbinic origin, we do not learn it from the statement of Rabbi Akiva, which deals with an invalidation by Torah law! However, one can say: even though it taught "added," if it had not taught it, it would not have taught us anything.

Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:7:2.hebrew: ואמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל אף צריך שיניח כו' - איצטריך לאיתויי דרב יהודה, משום דמינה דייקינן בגיטין דאתיא כרבי אלעזר, דאמר: עדי מסירה כרתי, דקי"ל כוותיה. ואיכא דמוקי לה התם כר"מ, ומפרש: מפני התקנה, משום קטטה; ולדידיה ליכא למידק מינה סתמא פסול:
Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:7:2.english: And Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says: He must also leave [the place of...], etc. — It was necessary to cite [this statement] of Rav Yehuda because from it we deduce in Gittin that [the mishna] follows Rabbi Elazar, who says that the witnesses of transmission effect the severance, and the halakha is in accordance with him. And there is [an amora] there who establishes it according to Rabbi Meir, and explains [that the requirement is merely] on account of an ordinance, due to [marital] strife; and according to him, one cannot deduce from it that [writing] without specification is invalid.

Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:9:1.hebrew: ואפילו לשם עובדת כוכבים נמי פסול - מדקתני "שנכתב שלא לשם אשה", דמשמע (על) [כל] נשים בכלל. ולא דמי ל"שלא לשמן" דכל הזבחים, דלא אמרינן "אפי' חולין בכלל", דהתם איכא לפרושי שנזבחו שלא לשם זבח זה, אלא לשם זבח אחר:
Tosafot on Zevachim 3a:9:1.english: "And even if it was for the sake of a gentile woman, it is also invalid" - Since [the mishna] teaches "that was written not for the sake of a woman," which implies that (on) [all] women are included. And this is not comparable to "not for their own sake" with regard to all the offerings, where we do not say that even non-sacred animals are included, because there it is possible to explain that they were slaughtered not for the sake of this offering, but rather for the sake of a different offering.

Zevachim 2b:3.english: Ravina said to Rav Pappa: Since you were not with us last night within the Shabbat limit of Bei Ḥarmakh, you did not hear that Rava raises a contradiction between two superior Mishnayot and teaches their resolution.

Zevachim 3a:11.english: Ravina continued to inform Rav Pappa of Rava’s statements: Rava further raises another contradiction: Did Rav Yehuda say that Rav says that a sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is unfit, whereas if one slaughtered the animal for the sake of ordinary meat, it is fit? Apparently, Rav holds that only improper intent that is of its type, i.e., for the sake of another offering, disqualifies the offering, whereas wrong intent that is not of its type, i.e., for the sake of ordinary meat, is disregarded and does not disqualify the offering.

Zevachim 3a:8.english: Ravina continued to inform Rav Pappa of Rava’s statements: Rava further raises another contradiction: Did Rav Yehuda say that Rav says that a sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is unfit, whereas if one slaughtered the sin offering for the sake of non-sacred meat, it is fit? Apparently, only improper intent that is of its type, i.e., for the sake of another offering, ruins the sin offering and renders it unfit, whereas wrong intent that is not of its type, i.e., for the sake of non-sacred meat, is disregarded and does not ruin the sin offering.
